Dior.summaryEn: A French luxury house whose fragrance range in Japan includes longstanding classics and the Sauvage collection.

Maison Margiela.nameJa: メゾン マルジェラ
Maison Margiela.summaryEn: A French fashion house whose REPLICA fragrances connect scent with places, moments and memories.

Le Labo.summaryEn: A fragrance house known for formulas named after a leading note and the number of materials in the composition.

Jo Malone.nameJa: ジョー マローン ロンドン
Jo Malone.summaryEn: A British fragrance house known for colognes designed to be worn alone or combined through scent layering.

Aesop.summaryEn: An Australian brand offering fragrance alongside skin, hair and body care in Japan.

Chanel.summaryEn: A French luxury house with fragrance lines ranging from classic chypres to contemporary woody and floral compositions.

Diptyque.summaryEn: A Paris fragrance house offering eaux de toilette, eaux de parfum and scented objects through its Japan site.

Tom Ford.summaryEn: A US luxury beauty brand whose fragrance range includes both signature scents and Private Blend creations.

Creed.summaryEn: A fragrance house whose current official catalogue includes Aventus and other woody, aromatic compositions.

Prada.summaryEn: An Italian fashion house with fragrance collections spanning clean iris, aromatic and gourmand styles.

J-Scent.summaryEn: A Japanese fragrance house built around wa no kaori — scents drawn from everyday Japanese life. Roasted green tea, sumo wrestler hair oil, paper soap, rakugan sweets. Because parent company LUZ manufactures in-house, J-Scent can pursue subjects most brands would not attempt. Every eau de parfum comes in the same 50 mL bottle at the same price, so the choice rests entirely on the scent.

KITOWA.summaryEn: Japan's first fragrance maison, launched in 2018 by Nippon Kodo, an incense house with 450 years of history. Every scent is built on natural oils from Japanese timber — hinoki from Mie, hiba from Aomori, kusunoki from Yakushima — layered with fine perfumery materials. The alcohol-free Eau Éclosion line uses a water base, unusual among luxury fragrances.

SHIRO.summaryEn: A Japanese cosmetics house from Sunagawa in Hokkaido, founded in 2009 as LAUREL and renamed SHIRO in 2019. Its fragrances are built around ingredients sourced from specific parts of Japan — sake lees from Kuriyama, gagome kelp from the waters off Hakodate, yuzu from Kito in Tokushima. Everything from formulation to retail is handled in-house, and the factory remains in Hokkaido.
